stem: What is the purpose of the organizing practice?
answer: To define and establish the project's structure of accountability and responsibilities
distractors: To define the products the project must deliver and their quality criteria
To establish why the project is worth doing and keep that justification under review
To define the management stages and the tolerances within which each one runs
To identify, assess and control the uncertainties that threaten the project's objectives
To set out how changes and other issues will be captured, assessed and controlled
To define the sequence of activities needed to deliver each specialist product
explanation: The organizing practice is concerned with the who: the structure of accountability and responsibilities. Products and quality belong to quality, justification to the business case, stages and tolerances to progress, uncertainty to risk, and changes to issues.

stem: The manual defines a role as a function assigned to a group or individual in a particular project. Which statement follows from that definition?
answer: A project role is not the same as the person's job outside the project
distractors: A project role must map one-to-one onto a job title in the organization
A project role is the set of tasks allocated to one named individual
A project role is the accountability that attaches to a board appointment
A project role describes the skills and experience a person must hold
A project role is a reporting line in the organization's line hierarchy
A project role is the employment contract under which the person works
explanation: The definition is explicit that a role is the function assigned within that project, not the person's position or job outside it. This is why someone whose job title is programme manager can hold the project executive role, and why job titles and project roles must be kept distinct.

stem: On a small project the project manager also carries out the team manager role. Which statement is correct?
answer: The roles may be combined, provided every responsibility in the method is still allocated
distractors: The roles may be combined only if the project board records the combination as an exception
The roles may be combined only when the project is using an iterative-incremental delivery method
Roles must always be allocated one-to-one to people, so the arrangement is not permitted
Responsibilities that are not allocated to a person may be left with the project board
The arrangement is permitted only if the project manager is not accountable for the business case
Combining roles is permitted, but the combined role must be recorded as a new tailored role
explanation: PRINCE2 defines roles and responsibilities, not tasks allocated one-to-one to people. Roles can be shared or combined within certain constraints according to the project's needs, but responsibilities must always be allocated. The constraint that matters here is the separation of the project manager from the executive and from assurance, not the team manager combination.

stem: Which set correctly pairs the three project interests with the roles PRINCE2 defines to represent them?
answer: Business with the project executive, user with the senior user, supplier with the senior supplier
distractors: Business with the senior user, user with the project executive, supplier with the senior supplier
Business with the project executive, user with the senior supplier, supplier with the senior user
Business with the project board, user with the senior user, supplier with the team manager
Business with the senior supplier, user with the senior user, supplier with the project executive
Business with the project executive, user with project assurance, supplier with the senior supplier
Business with the commissioning party, user with the senior user, supplier with the project manager
explanation: Table 6.1 pairs the interests with roles: the project executive represents the business viewpoint, the senior user represents user interests, and the senior supplier represents supplier interests. All three come together on the project board, which is accountable for the success of the project.

stem: A user group sits outside the organization and will operate the product after handover. Which interest do they represent, and which role represents it on the project?
answer: The user interest, represented by the senior user role on the board
distractors: The supplier interest, represented by the senior supplier role
The business interest, represented by the project executive role
The user interest, represented by the project assurance role
The business interest, represented by the senior user role
The supplier interest, represented by the operations manager role
The user interest, represented by the change authority role
explanation: Users can sit outside the business as end users or be impacted by the outputs of the project, and the senior user role represents them. Operations and maintenance interests normally sit with the senior user too, unless a different supplier provides those services.

stem: The manual says the three interests are brought together on the project board, and that the principle of manage by exception supports the day-to-day needs of managing the project. What does it say that principle enables?
answer: Decision-making at the most local level where the knowledge and capacity reside
distractors: A single decision-making point so that accountability cannot be diluted
Decisions being taken only at stage boundaries, when the board meets
Decisions being escalated to the commissioning party whenever a tolerance is threatened
The project board delegating all decisions to the project manager for the life of the project
Assurance being performed independently of the project manager at every level
The three interests each holding a veto over decisions that affect their community
explanation: Manage by exception is described here as enabling multi-layered decision-making at the most local level where the knowledge and capacity resides, which is what makes a board drawn from three communities workable rather than a bottleneck.

stem: Which organizational layer provides the project mandate and defines the project-level tolerances?
answer: Commissioning, the business layer
distractors: Directing, the project board
Managing, the project manager
Delivering, the team managers
The programme board, where the project sits within a programme
Project assurance, acting on behalf of the board
explanation: Table 6.2 gives the commissioning party four responsibilities: providing the project mandate, identifying the executive, defining the project-level tolerances the board will work within, and deciding whether to authorize a breach of a project-level tolerance.

stem: A forecast breach of a stage tolerance is escalated and the project board authorizes the deviation. A separate forecast breach threatens a project-level tolerance. Who decides whether to authorize that one?
answer: The commissioning party in the business layer, if appointed
distractors: The project board, because it directs the project
The project manager, because they manage the project day to day
The change authority, because it reports to the project board
The programme manager, because all tolerances roll up to programme level
Project assurance, because it acts independently of the project manager
The senior user, because the breach affects the user community
explanation: The layers divide tolerance decisions. The board determines deviations that breach or are forecast to breach stage tolerances; authorizing a breach of a project-level tolerance belongs to the commissioning party that set it.

stem: Which of these is NOT a responsibility of the directing layer?
answer: Defining the project-level tolerances for the project
distractors: Setting stage tolerances for each stage of the project
Authorizing the start and completion of each stage
Being accountable for the success of the project
explanation: Defining project-level tolerances is a commissioning responsibility. The directing layer works within those tolerances and sets stage tolerances, authorizes stage starts and completions, and is accountable for the project's success.

stem: What is described as the project manager's primary responsibility at the managing layer?
answer: Managing relationships so the project produces the products in line with objectives
distractors: Being accountable to the business for the success of the project
Deciding whether to authorize a deviation from the agreed stage tolerances
Taking day-to-day decisions for their own element of the project within the project manager's constraints
Providing the project mandate and identifying the project executive
Assuring the project board independently of the project manager, on the business
Determining the project-level tolerances and the change budget
explanation: The managing layer runs the project day to day within the board's constraints, and its primary responsibility is managing relationships so products meet the strategic objectives and agreed requirements such as quality, sustainability, time, cost, scope, benefits and risk goals.

stem: A specialist adviser attends workshops and contributes expertise, but is not on the project board, is not a team manager, and holds no assurance or support duties. Which statement is correct?
answer: The adviser is part of the project team but not the project management team
distractors: The adviser is part of both the project team and the project management team
The adviser is part of the project management team but not the project team
The adviser is part of neither, because they allocate no time to the project
The adviser is part of the project board as an informed member
The adviser must be represented by the senior supplier as a supplier interest
The adviser is part of the project ecosystem but outside the project team
explanation: PRINCE2 uses project team to cover all people required to allocate their time to the project, which is wider than the project management team. The management team structure is composed of the project board, project manager, team managers, and the project assurance and project support roles.

stem: Which list is the project management team structure?
answer: The project board, project manager, team managers, project assurance and project support
distractors: The project board and the project manager only, with assurance and support provided by the business
The project board, project manager and team members, with no assurance or support roles at all
The project manager, team managers, project support and the senior supplier's representative
The project board, project manager and project assurance, with no team managers or support
The project board, project manager, team managers and project support, but without assurance
The project board, project manager, team managers and project assurance, but without support
explanation: The definition names five components: project board, project manager, team managers, project assurance and project support. Missing either assurance or support from the list leaves the structure incomplete.

stem: Which role combination is explicitly prohibited for the project executive?
answer: Combining the project executive role with the project manager role
distractors: Combining the project executive role with the senior user role
Combining the project executive role with the senior supplier role
Combining the senior user role with the senior supplier role
Combining the project manager role with the team manager role
Combining the project manager role with the project support role
Combining a project board role with a project assurance role
explanation: There cannot be more than one project executive, and the role cannot be combined with the project manager role. On smaller projects the executive may be combined with the senior user or senior supplier; combining user and supplier is not recommended rather than prohibited, and the project manager may also perform team manager or support roles.

stem: An organization runs a job-sharing scheme and two people share the business role that corresponds to project executive. What does the manual say must happen?
answer: The business role still maps one-to-one to the project role, keeping a single point of accountability
distractors: Two project executive roles are created so that each job holder has one, each with half of the authority
The project executive role passes to the senior user while the job share continues, with the board's approval
Accountability is delegated to the project manager for the duration of the job share
The project must appoint an executive from outside the job-sharing scheme, and release the two job holders
The job share is not permitted, because the executive role cannot be shared in any form, even in part
The two job holders alternate accountability at each stage boundary, and each signs the stage report
explanation: The manual accepts job-sharing schemes but insists on a one-to-one allocation of the business role to the project role, with additional arrangements to make clear how the single point of accountability is maintained. Those arrangements should be reflected in the executive's role description and the project initiation documentation.

stem: Which of these is NOT a responsibility of the senior user?
answer: Securing funding for the project and owning the business case
distractors: Ensuring the approach gains user buy-in to the project
Monitoring the products against the requirements in line with the business case
Controlling change to requirements and benefits
explanation: Funding and ownership of the business case belong to the project executive. The senior user is accountable for how user requirements are captured and benefits specified, and for buy-in, monitoring against requirements, controlling change to requirements and benefits, and handover and adoption.

stem: Benefits from a project will continue to be realized for two years after the project closes. Who is responsible for the continued realization of those benefits after closure?
answer: The senior user
distractors: The project executive
The project manager
The business change manager
Project assurance
The team manager who delivered the products
explanation: The senior user is responsible for successful handover and adoption of products into the business and for the continued realization of benefits after the project has closed, including securing ongoing commitment from the user community where that commitment outlasts the project.

stem: Which role is accountable for the quality of the products delivered by suppliers and for the technical integrity of the project?
answer: The senior supplier
distractors: The project manager
The project executive
The senior user
The team manager
Project assurance
The design authority
explanation: The senior supplier represents the supplier community across all aspects of delivery, ensures sufficient ongoing commitment of supplier people and resources, and is accountable for the quality of supplier-delivered products and the project's technical integrity.

stem: Maintenance of a project's products will be provided after closure by the business's own internal IT department, not by the delivery supplier. Who is more likely to represent those operations and maintenance interests?
answer: The senior user
distractors: The senior supplier
The project executive
The project manager
Project assurance
The IT department manager acting as senior supplier
The team manager responsible for support
explanation: The senior supplier normally represents maintenance interests, but the manual notes the exception where maintenance is provided by the business, such as an internal IT department, or is outsourced elsewhere. In that case operations and maintenance interests are more likely to be represented by a senior user. What matters is that those interests are represented from the outset.

stem: Which combination of project board roles is not recommended, because it creates conflicts of interest in decision-making?
answer: Combining the senior user and senior supplier roles
distractors: Combining the project executive and senior user roles
Combining the project executive and senior supplier roles
Combining the project manager and team manager roles
Combining the project manager and project support roles
Combining a board role with a project assurance role
Combining two senior user roles on a large project
explanation: On smaller projects the executive may be combined with the senior user or senior supplier. Combining the senior user and senior supplier is not recommended, to avoid conflicts of interest and to keep both communities adequately represented in decision-making.

stem: Which of these is NOT a project board responsibility?
answer: Authorizing each work package before it is issued to a team manager
distractors: Setting stage tolerances to enable management by exception
Establishing the tolerances and the change budget
Assuring all aspects of the project's performance and products independently of the project manager
explanation: Work packages are allocated by the project manager to team managers. The board's responsibilities include setting stage tolerances, establishing tolerances and the change budget, assuring performance and products independently of the project manager, and creating the conditions for the project to succeed.

stem: Which of these is NOT part of the project manager's responsibility?
answer: Authorizing a deviation that breaches an agreed stage tolerance
distractors: Setting work package tolerances for team managers
Delegating work to team managers or team members where appropriate
Ensuring decisions are made in line with project board guidance and tolerances
explanation: The project manager runs the project within the tolerances set by the board. A breach or forecast breach of a stage tolerance is escalated, because authorizing the deviation is the board's decision. Setting work package tolerances, delegating work and keeping decisions within board guidance are all project manager responsibilities.

stem: A project manager proposes to take on the project assurance role as well, to save cost on a small project. Why does the method not allow this?
answer: Assurance must be independent of the project manager, so they cannot take it
distractors: Because the project manager lacks the authority to assure the project board
Because assurance must always be performed by a project board member personally
Because the project manager may not hold more than one project role of any kind
Because the assurance role must be filled on a full-time basis
Because assurance for a small project must come from an external party
Because the board must appoint assurance before the project manager is appointed
explanation: Project assurance roles cannot be assigned to the project manager, team manager, project team members or project support. The purpose is independence: assurance gives the board a view of performance and products that does not come from the person managing the work.

stem: How is work allocated to a team manager?
answer: As a work package, in line with the commercial management approach
distractors: As a stage plan, authorized by the project board for the stage
As a project brief, issued at the start of the project to every team
Verbally at each progress checkpoint, and confirmed in the next report
Through the project board, at the end of each stage, in the stage report
As a request for change, raised by the team manager after the stage begins
As a product description, agreed with project assurance for each product
explanation: The project manager allocates work to a team manager in the form of a work package, in line with the commercial management approach. The team manager then delivers the products to the agreed specifications within the tolerances and constraints agreed with the project manager.

stem: A self-organizing agile team agrees that the team manager role will be held collectively by the whole team, with one member acting as the project manager's single point of contact. What does the method require for this to be acceptable?
answer: The team must hold all the team manager responsibilities, and the arrangement be accepted as tailoring
distractors: A named individual must still hold the team manager role on the project board's behalf
The project manager must take on the team manager responsibilities personally, and report to the board
The team must adopt the PRINCE2 role names before the arrangement can be used, and the board must agree
The arrangement must be approved by the commissioning party as a project-level tolerance change
The team manager role cannot be tailored, because it is required on every project, and by every team
Project assurance must cover the team manager responsibilities in the absence of a named holder
explanation: The manual's scenario accepts collective ownership: every area of the team manager's responsibility becomes the responsibility of the whole team and each member, a single point of contact is appointed for the project manager, and the project manager accepts it as appropriate tailoring at team level.

stem: A project board delegates its assurance tasks to a specialist from the wider business. Who remains accountable for that assurance?
answer: The project board member whose area of concern is being assured
distractors: The specialist who performs the assurance tasks
The project manager, because they run the project day to day
The project executive alone, because they are accountable for the project
Project support, because it administers the assurance schedule
The commissioning party, because it appointed the board
The assurance provider's line manager in the wider business
explanation: Board members are accountable for assurance of their own areas of concern. Assurance tasks may be done by the board member, by someone appointed from the wider business, or by an external party, but where the roles are delegated the respective board member remains accountable.

stem: A project manager proposes that the project support officer also carry out business assurance, since they already attend every board meeting. Why is this not permitted?
answer: Project support must stay separate from assurance to keep assurance independent
distractors: Because the support officer is unlikely to have the skills needed for assurance, or the time to learn them
Because assurance must be performed by a member of the project board
Because the executive must approve every assurance appointment
Because assurance of the business interest is a supplier responsibility
Because the support officer does not allocate enough time to the project
Because assurance tasks can only be delegated to an external party
explanation: The method is explicit that project support must be kept separate from project assurance to maintain the independence of assurance, and that assurance roles cannot be assigned to the project manager, team managers, project team members or project support.

stem: Who is responsible for the project support role, and can it be delegated?
answer: The project manager is responsible, and may delegate it to suppliers, individuals or groups
distractors: The project board is responsible, and may delegate it only to a project office, or to the executive
The project executive is responsible, and may delegate it only within the business, or to the sponsor
The project manager is responsible, and may not delegate it at all, even to a project office
The senior supplier is responsible, and may delegate it to supplier staff, or to the team managers
Project assurance is responsible, and may delegate it to the project office, or to the executive
The commissioning party is responsible, and may delegate it to a P3O, or to a programme office
explanation: Project support is the project manager's responsibility but can be delegated to suppliers, individuals, groups within the business or other team members, depending on scale, complexity, and the project manager's skills, knowledge and capacity. A project office can fulfil the role.

stem: An organization's project office provides planning support, change administration and facilitation of workshops for a project. Which role is it fulfilling?
answer: Project support
distractors: Project assurance
The project manager
The change authority
The team manager
Programme governance
The senior user
explanation: Project support provides services such as administrative support, facilitating meetings and workshops, advice and guidance on project tools, planning support, and risk, issue and change management. Some organizations establish a project office that fulfils this role.

stem: What does the work breakdown structure link?
answer: The product breakdown structure and the work packages
distractors: The project plan and the stage plans
The business case and the benefits management approach
The project management team structure and the role descriptions
The product breakdown structure and the product descriptions
Each stage boundary and the end stage report
The delivery model and the commercial management approach
explanation: The work breakdown structure is a hierarchy of all the work to be done, and forms the link between the product breakdown structure and the work packages, helping the project manager decide how to structure teams and where their boundaries should fall.

stem: A project consists of a single work package delivered by a small team. What does the manual say about the work breakdown structure?
answer: It would not be required for a project as simple as this
distractors: It is required whenever any external supplier is involved
It is required whenever the project has more than three teams
It is required to establish the stage tolerances
It is a mandatory part of the project initiation documentation
It is required whenever the product breakdown structure has more than one level
It is required before a work package can be authorized
explanation: The manual says the work breakdown structure is most useful with multiple work packages, particularly a mix of internally staffed and externally supplied ones. For a very simple project, such as delivery of one work package with a small team, it would not be required.

stem: Why does the manual advise against a single work package containing both internal and external team members?
answer: An internal agreement and an external contract have a different character and set of relationships
distractors: External team members cannot be given work package tolerances, and the contract forbids any mixing
A work package may only be issued to a single supplier organization, and to one named team manager only
The commercial management approach forbids mixed teams on any project, and the board must not approve them
The work breakdown structure requires one work package per supplier, and one team manager per package
Internal staff cannot be managed by a team manager from a supplier, and vice versa, in any project
Mixed work packages cannot be assured by the project board, and so cannot be authorized by the manager
explanation: The manual's reason is the difference in kind between an internal agreement and an external contract, and the relationships that go with each. It is better to manage them separately rather than place both inside one work package.

stem: Which sequence is the PRINCE2 technique for organizational design and development?
answer: Understand the organizational ecosystem, design the project ecosystem, develop it, manage changes to it, then transition it into the organization
distractors: Design the project ecosystem, understand the organizational ecosystem, transition the project, develop the project ecosystem, then manage changes to it
Understand the organizational ecosystem, develop the project ecosystem, design the project ecosystem, transition the project, then manage changes to it
Design the project ecosystem, develop the project ecosystem, understand the organizational ecosystem, manage changes to it, then transition the project
Understand the organizational ecosystem, design the project ecosystem, transition the project, manage changes to it, then develop the project ecosystem
Develop the project ecosystem, understand the organizational ecosystem, design the project ecosystem, manage changes to it, then transition the project
Understand the organizational ecosystem, transition the project, design the project ecosystem, develop the project ecosystem, then manage changes to it
explanation: The five steps run in a deliberate order: understand the ecosystem the project is joining, design the project ecosystem, develop it, manage ongoing changes to it, and finally transition the project back into the organizational ecosystem.

stem: A business already has its own organizational design procedure and wants to use it instead of the PRINCE2 technique. What does the method require?
answer: It should be documented as a tailoring decision in the initiation documentation
distractors: The alternative must be approved by the project board in an end stage report
An alternative procedure is not permitted, because the technique is mandatory
The alternative must be raised as a request for change and assessed by the change authority
The alternative must be recorded in the lessons log at the end of the project
The alternative must be agreed with the commissioning party as a project-level tolerance
The alternative may be used only if it covers all five steps of the PRINCE2 technique
explanation: An alternative procedure can be used, but its use should be documented as part of the tailoring decisions in the project initiation documentation, so the choice is visible and reviewable rather than implicit.

stem: When understanding the organizational ecosystem, the project approach should make clear who retains responsibility for several things. Which of these is NOT one of them?
answer: The quality criteria for each specialist product in the stage plan
distractors: People management, such as performance management, rewards and wellbeing
Which decisions are subject to corporate governance
How and when project team members transition on and off the project
explanation: The four areas listed are people management, governance, management approaches such as policies and ways of working, and how and when team members transition on and off the project. Quality criteria belong to the quality practice.

stem: Who is responsible for the project organizational design, and where is it documented?
answer: The project executive, supported by the project manager, documented in the initiation documentation
distractors: The project manager alone, documented in the stage plan, and approved by the board before initiation
The project board collectively, documented in the project mandate, and approved by the business layer
The programme manager, documented in the programme plan, and then copied into the project brief
Project assurance, documented in the assurance plan
The commissioning party, documented in the business case, and confirmed by the corporate body
The project support role, documented in the communication management approach, and issued to the team
explanation: The executive, supported by the project manager, is responsible for the project organizational design, and it should be documented in the project initiation documentation. On large or complex projects the executive may delegate it internally or to a specialist supplier.

stem: A project will move from a client-led design team to a supplier-led delivery team at stage 3. What does the manual say should happen during initiation?
answer: The transition should be identified and planned, with team structures planned for the different stages
distractors: The structure should stay fixed, because changes to the team structure require a new project mandate
The supplier-led structure should be deferred until the stage boundary, when it can be designed
The design team should be retained alongside the delivery team to avoid loss of knowledge
The transition should be raised as an exception once the stage begins, and then planned by the new team
The project board should appoint the delivery team before the design stage starts, and release the designers
The change should be recorded in the lessons log rather than planned in advance, and reviewed at closure
explanation: Where the structure needs to change between stages, this should where possible be identified and planned during initiation, establishing planned team structures at different stages, and considering the people and resources needed to support the transition and its impact on the team.

stem: Which of these is NOT a project organizational development activity?
answer: Setting the stage tolerances for the next stage at the boundary
distractors: Onboarding people to the project through induction or certification
Running skills and capability assessments of the project team
Succession planning, recognizing that people may leave before completion
explanation: Development covers onboarding, skills assessment, training, team building, establishing a project culture, succession planning and offboarding to capture lessons. Stage tolerances are set by the project board as part of directing the project.

topic: Manage changes to the project ecosystem
stem: Mid-stage, a team member's capability gap becomes clear and the work they hold is at risk. Which response matches the project manager's responsibility for managing the project ecosystem?
answer: Match responsibilities to capability by sourcing skills, coaching, or reallocating the work
distractors: Raise an exception immediately, because any capability gap breaches the stage tolerances
Ask the project board to replace the team member at the next stage boundary
Amend the business case to reflect the reduced capability of the team, and the likely delay
Re-plan the stage so that the affected work moves to a later stage, and tell the board
Ask project assurance to cover the work until someone else is available, and report back
Record the gap in the lessons log and continue with the original allocation, whatever the risk
explanation: The project manager is responsible for making the best use of the people and resources available: matching responsibilities to capability and capacity, sourcing additional skills, or upskilling through coaching and learning, with the commercial management approach supporting people moving on and off the project.

stem: Which three aspects does the project board need to consider when transitioning the project into the organizational ecosystem?
answer: Products, people and learning
distractors: Products, budget and contracts
People, processes and technology
Learning, benefits and risk
Products, suppliers and benefits
People, governance and reporting
Products, people and performance
explanation: The three aspects are products (accepted by the business and owned afterwards, including further development, benefits monitoring and maintenance), people (transitioned back into the business or managed under supplier arrangements), and learning (sharing lessons and using knowledge gained).

stem: What distinguishes a thin client delivery model from a thick client model?
answer: In a thin client model most of the work, including much of the project management, is undertaken by external suppliers
distractors: In a thin client model most of the work is undertaken by the business, with suppliers supplying only specialist skills
In a thin client model all project management is retained in-house while delivery is outsourced to suppliers
In a thin client model the project board is chaired by the senior supplier, who also approves the stages
In a thin client model work is contracted on a labor basis only, with suppliers paid by the day worked
In a thin client model the business retains responsibility for supplier performance and for all delivery
In a thin client model there is no senior supplier role on the project board, and no supplier assurance
explanation: Delivery models range from thin client, where most project work and much of the management work is done by external suppliers, to thick client, where most is done by the business. The model defines which aspects of project management are in-house or external.

stem: A supplier is engaged on a labor basis rather than a product basis. Who is generally responsible for the performance of the work?
answer: The client, because it directs the work
distractors: The supplier, because it employs the workers
The client and supplier jointly, in equal shares
The project board, as a collective body
The senior supplier, on the board's behalf
The team manager, whichever organization they come from
explanation: The manual draws the distinction directly: contracting on a labor basis means the client generally remains responsible for the performance of the work, whereas on a product basis the supplier remains responsible for their performance.

stem: Who determines the balance between in-house and external suppliers and the commercial arrangements between them?
answer: The project board, in consultation with the project manager
distractors: The project manager, in consultation with the team managers
The commissioning party, in consultation with the project executive
The senior supplier, in consultation with the supplier organizations
Project assurance, in consultation with the project board
The project support role, in consultation with procurement
The programme manager, in consultation with the business change manager
explanation: The board, in consultation with the project manager, determines the right balance between in-house and external suppliers and the commercial arrangements required, and this is captured in the commercial management approach.

stem: In a RACI chart, what does the accountable designation mean?
answer: The single person who owns the task or the outcome
distractors: One or more people who perform the task
The people whose input is required for the task
The people who are informed of progress or completion
The most senior person with an interest in the task
The person who authorizes the budget for the task
The person who assures the task on the board's behalf
explanation: RACI stands for responsible (one or more people who perform the task), accountable (the single person who owns it), consulted (those whose input is required) and informed (those told of progress or completion).

stem: Which of these is given as an example of integrating programme and project roles?
answer: A single programme office taking project support duties for all projects
distractors: Each project having a board with no members in common with any other project
The programme manager being barred from acting as a project executive
A business change manager being barred from the senior user role
Stage boundaries being staggered so that no two projects review at the same time
Project assurance being provided by the programme office for all projects
Each project appointing its own support office independent of the programme
explanation: Integration examples include the programme manager acting as project executive for one or more projects, multiple boards or a single directing body, a business change manager fulfilling senior user, and a single programme office taking project support for all projects. The aim is clear lines of responsibility, no duplication, and efficient reporting and reviews.

stem: An iterative-incremental delivery method includes a product owner role. Which PRINCE2 role could it be aligned to?
answer: The senior user
distractors: The project executive
The senior supplier
The team manager
Project assurance
The business change manager
The change authority
explanation: The manual gives the product owner as an example where a simple change of terminology and minor amendments to the role description may suffice, aligning it to the senior user role. Where roles do not map so neatly, distinct roles may be added with agreement on how they relate to the PRINCE2 roles.

stem: Accountability for sustainability targets should be captured in several places. Which of these is NOT one of them?
answer: The daily log
distractors: The business case
The requirement setting
People's role descriptions
explanation: The manual calls for clear accountability for sustainability targets across the project ecosystem, captured in the business case, the requirement setting and people's role descriptions. The project management team structure and role descriptions should also define responsibilities, including how targets are managed after the project concludes.

stem: A large project establishes a change authority, distinct from the project manager, reporting to the project board. Where is its use and composition documented?
answer: The issue management approach
distractors: The commercial management approach
The change management approach
The communication management approach
The project initiation documentation only
The stage plan for the current stage
The risk management approach
explanation: The change authority is a way for the board to delegate authority to approve requests for change or off-specification, aligned to the agreed project tolerances. Its use and composition are documented in the issue management approach.

stem: Which management product describes the delivery model for the project work, such as which elements of the work breakdown structure will be delivered by external suppliers?
answer: The commercial management approach
distractors: The project management team structure
The role descriptions
The communication management approach
The project approach
The issue management approach
The work breakdown structure itself
explanation: The commercial management approach covers the procedures, techniques, standards and responsibilities for commercial management, including market engagement, procurement and contract management, and it contains the delivery model. The work breakdown structure is an input to that decision, not the description of it.

stem: Which of these is NOT high-level content of the project management team structure management product?
answer: The quality criteria for each specialist product in the stage plan
distractors: A chart showing the structure of the team and their reporting lines
A summary of authority and responsibilities, possibly in matrix form
Working practices such as co-location or arrangements for remote teams
explanation: The product defines who is involved in the project, their relationships and how they will work together: the structure chart, a summary of authority and responsibilities, working practices, and supporting information on other key personnel and relationships. Quality criteria belong to product descriptions.

stem: Which organizing responsibility belongs to the business layer rather than to the project executive?
answer: Appointing the project executive, and possibly the project manager
distractors: Approving the commercial management approach, and its procedures
Confirming appointments to the project management team
Approving the project management team structure, and its design
Preparing the role descriptions, and agreeing them with the team
Assuring the implementation of the commercial management procedures
explanation: Table 6.4 splits the responsibilities. The business layer appoints the executive and possibly the project manager, provides the business's communications standards, and provides information as defined in the communication management approach. Approving the commercial management approach and confirming team appointments are executive responsibilities.

stem: Which role prepares the role descriptions and designs, reviews and updates the project management team structure?
answer: The project manager
distractors: The project executive
The project board collectively
Project assurance
Project support
The business layer
The team manager
explanation: The project manager prepares and updates the commercial, communication and change management approaches, designs, reviews and updates the team structure and work breakdown structure, prepares role descriptions, and maintains a healthy project ecosystem. The executive approves the structure, and assurance advises and confirms compliance.

stem: Which outcome does the organizing practice produce in support of the principle define roles, responsibilities and relationships?
answer: There is no duplication or gap in responsibilities, and relationships are positive across the ecosystem
distractors: The project is able to adapt to changing business needs, and decisions align with the business case
The right people are in the right roles at the right time, and are able to deliver the project on schedule
The project can evolve at stage boundaries, and appropriate skills are deployed at each stage of delivery
Decision-making is timely, and accountability and ownership of actions are increased across the team
Products are more readily accepted by users, and brought into operational use without delay or rework
An effective team structure is created, and is appropriately sized for the project and its risk profile
explanation: Table 6.5 pairs the principle with the mechanism (developing an explicit team structure so everyone is aware of their responsibilities and relationships) and the result: no duplication of or gap in responsibilities, positive relationships across the ecosystem, and between the project and those it affects.
